reasons.plausibility: The hypothesis incorrectly links low stacking fault energy to enhanced cross-slip and reduced work hardening; low SFE actually suppresses cross-slip and promotes planar slip and higher work hardening, contradicting well-established physical metallurgy principles.
reasons.testability: The proposed test is detailed and would be decisive, but it is built on a physically incorrect premise, so the test as described would not properly evaluate the intended mechanism.
reasons.usefulness: The hypothesis is not useful because it is based on a fundamental misunderstanding of stacking fault energy effects, and pursuing it would misdirect research effort.
